punctuated: 功，斯其爲真任事也已矣。夫喜事似任，任事似畏。而喜者，生事者也；畏者，諉事者也；任者，行所無事者也。其重如弩持，非畏也；其輕如鷙發，非喜也。此不可不察也。牧、充國雖不先衆議，而議者卒屈焉；度若魯雖與衆抗議，而議者莫能難焉。故好議非也，因而廢議亦非也；議而能成，何惡於議？此又不可不察也。雖然，有任事者，有任任事者。今海内無事，天子垂意四顧，不愛高位厚祿，懸以待天下，若曰：「今獨不得牧、充國爲將，度往視師，魯爲河防使耳，何憂北胡、西羌、東南山海之寇、河淮之漕哉！」愚戇不知忌諱，竊以爲誠出魯之計，不爲行河者報罷乎？出度之計，不爲言師老財匱者沮乎？出充國與牧之計，辛武賢不見代乎？縱虜不下廷尉乎？即成功，不有以日費市租、久留天誅議其後者乎？如此，即令四臣在事，掣肘無益也。是故
translation_en: … credit for the achievement—this indeed is truly shouldering responsibility for affairs! Now, being fond of meddling resembles shouldering responsibility, and shouldering responsibility resembles timidity. Yet those who are fond of meddling stir up trouble; those who are timid shirk responsibility; and those who shoulder responsibility act effortlessly without creating trouble. When they are as cautious as a drawn crossbow being held steady, it is not out of timidity; when they are as swift as a bird of prey striking, it is not out of a fondness for meddling. This must be carefully examined. Although Li Mu 李牧 and Zhao Chongguo 趙充國 did not initially follow the consensus of court deliberations, the deliberators eventually yielded to them; although Pei Du 裴度 and Jia Lu 賈魯 argued against the crowd, none of the deliberators could refute them. Therefore, to be overly fond of deliberations is wrong, yet to abolish deliberations because of that is also wrong; if deliberation can lead to success, why despise deliberation? This, too, must be carefully examined. Even so, there are those who shoulder responsibility for affairs, and there are those who entrust others with shouldering responsibility for affairs. Today all within the seas is at peace, and the Son of Heaven turns his attention to look all around, not grudging high office and generous emoluments, holding them out as he awaits the talents of the realm, as if to say: "Today we simply cannot get men like Li Mu and Zhao Chongguo as generals, Pei Du to go inspect the armies, or Jia Lu to serve as River Defense Commissioner (hefang shi); otherwise, what worry would there be over the northern Hu, the western Qiang, the bandits of the southeastern mountains and seas, or the grain transport along the Yellow and Huai rivers!" In my foolish bluntness, ignorant of taboos, I privately believe that if a plan like Jia Lu's were truly put forward today, would it not be reported back and canceled by those inspecting the river? If a plan like Pei Du's were put forward, would it not be blocked by those claiming the troops are exhausted and finances depleted? If a plan like Zhao Chongguo's or Li Mu's were put forward, would someone like Xin Wuxian 辛武賢 not be appointed to replace him? Would he not be handed over to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement (tingwei) for letting the enemy escape? Even if he succeeded, would there not be critics afterward impeaching him for daily squandering market taxes or long delaying heavenly punishment? If things are like this, even if those four ministers were in office today, their elbows would be held back and it would be of no avail. Therefore, …

title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
披腹心去形迹寛文法假便宜寄以專閫
謗書盈篋不視也授以竒策捐金恣所出
不問也責以實效不貲之賞不次之擢不
靳也此任任事者也然要在知人得其人
而專任者成非其人而專任者敗此又不
可不察也乃人臣之自任則有可言者夫
臨事而不度理之所當則謬度理矣而不
度勢之所至則迂度勢矣而不度時之所
宜則泥度時矣而不度已之所能則妄懷
===
選愞之私托之乎慎重則李趙接踵矣覬
徼倖之獲托之乎伉慨則裴賈比肩矣吾
所避難以觀望左右而左右者復然吾所
召釁以留遺後來而後來者復然天下事
誰當任之者愚未明世務嘗觀前史淮陰
武士隆中逸民皆立談之頃為世主畫大
計終身所就卒如其言傳曰心誠求之不
中不遠患心之不誠豈患不中哉執事幸
開承學各量所自任以意對敢不盡其愚

punctuated: 披腹心、去形迹、寛文法、假便宜；寄以專閫，謗書盈篋不視也；授以竒策，捐金恣所出不問也；責以實效，不貲之賞、不次之擢不靳也。此任任事者也。然要在知人：得其人而專任者成，非其人而專任者敗，此又不可不察也。乃人臣之自任，則有可言者。夫臨事而不度理之所當則謬，度理矣而不度勢之所至則迂，度勢矣而不度時之所宜則泥，度時矣而不度已之所能則妄。懷選愞之私，托之乎慎重，則李、趙接踵矣；覬徼倖之獲，托之乎伉慨，則裴、賈比肩矣。吾所避難以觀望左右，而左右者復然；吾所召釁以留遺後來，而後來者復然：天下事誰當任之者？愚未明世務，嘗觀前史：淮陰武士、隆中逸民，皆立談之頃為世主畫大計，終身所就，卒如其言。《傳》曰：「心誠求之，不中不遠。」患心之不誠，豈患不中哉？執事幸開承學，各量所自任以意對，敢不盡其愚！
translation_en:
…laying bare one's heart and mind, setting aside outward formalities, relaxing the letter of the law, and granting discretionary authority; entrusting them with sole command outside the capital, while ignoring a chestful of slanderous letters; empowering them to carry out extraordinary strategies, and lavishing gold for them to spend at will without asking questions; demanding actual results of them, and not begrudging immeasurable rewards or out-of-turn promotions—this is how one entrusts those who take on affairs. Yet the key lies in knowing men: if one finds the right man and gives him sole responsibility, he succeeds; if one gives sole responsibility to the wrong man, he fails. This, too, cannot go unexamined.

As for how a minister takes responsibility upon himself, there is also something to be said. When confronting an affair, if one does not measure what principle requires, one is in error; if one measures principle yet does not measure where the trend of circumstances leads, one is impractical; if one measures the circumstances yet does not measure what is timely, one is rigid; and if one measures the times yet does not measure one's own capabilities, one is reckless. If those who harbor selfish timidity and irresolution cloak themselves in prudence, then men like Li Mu 李牧 and Zhao Chongguo 趙充國 would follow on each other's heels! If those who covet a lucky gain cloak themselves in high-spirited resolve, then men like Pei Du 裴度 and Jia Ru 賈魯 would stand shoulder to shoulder! If we shirk difficulties and look hesitantly to those around us, and those around us do the same; if we provoke troubles and leave them behind for those who come after, and those who come after do the same—then who is to take responsibility for the affairs of the realm?

Ignorant as I am of the affairs of the world, I have read the histories of former times: the warrior of Huaiyin [Han Xin 韓信] and the recluse of Longzhong [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] both mapped out grand strategies for the rulers of their ages in the space of a standing conversation, and what they accomplished over their lifetimes ultimately matched their words. The Commentary [the Great Learning (Daxue)] says: "If you seek it with a sincere heart, though you may not hit the mark, you will not be far off." One should worry that the heart is not sincere; why worry about not hitting the mark? Since Your Excellency has graciously invited us students to measure what we would take upon ourselves and reply with our own thoughts, how dare I not pour out the whole of my humble folly!

title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第四問
楊汝翰
同考試官進士張批久任法行我
國家復古一大機也是篇能詳道變通之術真留心時務者
考試官右贊善許批策所陳六事可以佐久任之
議矣錄之以備採擇
考試官右中允何批久任本治世良法顧行之
有善不善耳此作得之蓋識時務者
嘗謂法無弗宜於今而人貴善師乎古則
===
今日之論久任是已夫法者本以存其大
綱而其出入變化固將付之於人用之而
善則人競效其官事各得其理而可以圖
萬世之安用之而不善通則徇時執則膠
故於是議者祗病法之拘而不見法之效
豈法之設端使然哉無亦行之者之過歟
且久任之法昉於唐虞備於成周而沿於
兩漢之盛際蓋三考乃行黜陟而居官至
長子孫故當其時治道蓁隆良吏為盛焉

第四問

楊汝翰

同考試官進士張批：久任法行，我國家復古一大機也。是篇能詳道變通之術，真留心時務者。

考試官右贊善許批：策所陳六事，可以佐久任之議矣。錄之以備採擇。

考試官右中允何批：久任本治世良法，顧行之有善不善耳。此作得之，蓋識時務者。

嘗謂法無弗宜於今，而人貴善師乎古，則今日之論久任是已。夫法者，本以存其大綱，而其出入變化，固將付之於人。用之而善，則人競效其官，事各得其理，而可以圖萬世之安；用之而不善，通則徇時，執則膠故，於是議者祗病法之拘，而不見法之效。豈法之設端使然哉？無亦行之者之過歟！且久任之法，昉於唐、虞，備於成周，而沿於兩漢之盛際。蓋三考乃行黜陟，而居官至長子孫，故當其時，治道蓁隆，良吏為盛焉。
translation_en:
Fourth Question

Yang Ruhan 楊汝翰

Associate Examiner, Metropolitan Graduate (jinshi) Zhang 張 comments: The implementation of the system of long tenure in office is a great opportunity for our dynasty to restore the ways of antiquity. This essay is able to set forth in detail the methods of flexible adaptation; the author truly pays close attention to current affairs.

Examiner, Right Admonisher Xu 許 comments: The six matters presented in this policy essay can aid the deliberations on long tenure in office. We record it here so that it may be available for selection and adoption.

Examiner, Right Companion He 何 comments: Long tenure in office is fundamentally a fine method for governing the world; it simply depends on whether it is carried out well or poorly. This piece has grasped this point, and its author is someone who understands current affairs.

I have always held that there is no institution that cannot be made suitable for the present, and that what is crucial in men is knowing how to take antiquity as a teacher—and today's discussion of long tenure in office is just such a case. Now, laws and institutions are fundamentally meant to preserve the overarching framework, while their adjustments and adaptations are naturally entrusted to men. When applied well, men vie to fulfill their official duties, affairs each attain their proper order, and one can plan for the peace of ten thousand generations; when applied poorly, flexibility turns into mere accommodation to the times, while strictness turns into stubborn adherence to old ruts. Thereupon, critics merely fault the institution for its rigidity and fail to see its efficacy. Could it be the original establishment of the institution that made it so? Is it not rather the fault of those who implement it! Moreover, the institution of long tenure in office began under Tang 唐 (Yao 堯) and Yu 虞 (Shun 舜), was perfected under the Zhou 周 dynasty, and was continued during the flourishing eras of the Former and Later Han 漢. Indeed, only after three triennial evaluations were demotions and promotions carried out, and officials remained in their posts long enough to raise children and grandchildren; therefore, in those times, the way of governance was lushly prosperous [?] and upright officials were abundant.

title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
嗣是言久任者蓋詳而致行之者寔鮮漢
王嘉朱浮左雄俱有守長數易之諫宋司
馬光宋祁陳靖俱有久任當行之請張方
平則勸仁宗以久任之效矣鄭剛中則開
高宗以不久任之弊矣夫豈不義而數子
言之蓋守長吏民之本師帥之官也官常
民俗非久不能諳其詳曲折委微非久不
能窮其變條畫措置非久不能竟其緒勞
能功閥非久不能驗其成任之而久則上
===
務精勤其職業而無苟且之思下知服從
其教化而有相安之美緣絶簿書之奸既
息送故迎新之費亦省任之而不久則傳
相促急各懷一切其擾則妨民其費則傷
民其無意於留而苟簡於治則病民其自
以為亟遷而求足其欲則又困民故久任
之為良法可坐而策也今
天子嘉惠黎元興起吏治
明詔秉銓之臣一以六期為斷蓋將漸復□□

punctuated:
嗣是，言久任者蓋詳，而致行之者寔鮮。漢王嘉、朱浮、左雄，俱有守長數易之諫；宋司馬光、宋祁、陳靖，俱有久任當行之請；張方平則勸仁宗以久任之效矣，鄭剛中則開高宗以不久任之弊矣。夫豈不義而數子言之？蓋守長，吏民之本，師帥之官也。官常民俗，非久不能諳其詳；曲折委微，非久不能窮其變；條畫措置，非久不能竟其緒；勞能功閥，非久不能驗其成。任之而久，則上務精勤其職業，而無苟且之思；下知服從其教化，而有相安之美。緣絶簿書之奸既息，送故迎新之費亦省。任之而不久，則傳相促急，各懷一切，其擾則妨民，其費則傷民，其無意於留而苟簡於治則病民，其自以為亟遷而求足其欲則又困民。故久任之為良法，可坐而策也。今
天子嘉惠黎元，興起吏治，明詔秉銓之臣，一以六期為斷，蓋將漸復□□
translation_en: Since then, those who have spoken of long tenure in office have done so in great detail, yet those who have actually put it into practice have been truly few. In the Han dynasty, Wang Jia 王嘉, Zhu Fu 朱浮, and Zuo Xiong 左雄 all submitted remonstrances against the frequent replacement of Grand Administrators and County Magistrates; in the Song dynasty, Sima Guang 司馬光, Song Qi 宋祁, and Chen Jing 陳靖 all submitted petitions urging that long tenure ought to be practiced; Zhang Fangping 張方平 exhorted Emperor Renzong 仁宗 regarding the effectiveness of long tenure, while Zheng Gangzhong 鄭剛中 enlightened Emperor Gaozong 高宗 regarding the abuses of short tenure. Could it be without righteous cause that these several gentlemen spoke of it? Indeed, Grand Administrators and County Magistrates are the foundation of clerks and the common people, and are officials who act as teachers and leaders. Without long tenure, one cannot become thoroughly familiar with the details of official routines and popular customs; without long tenure, one cannot exhaust the permutations of intricate and subtle complexities; without long tenure, one cannot carry through to completion the threads of planned regulations and administrative measures; without long tenure, one cannot verify the accomplishments of toil, ability, and accumulated merit. When officials are appointed for a long time, superiors devote themselves with diligence and precision to their duties without harboring thoughts of perfunctory makeshift, while subordinates know to obey their moral transformation and enjoy the beauty of mutual peace. Not only do the frauds of manipulating and severing official registers cease, but the expenses of sending off the old and welcoming the new are also saved. When officials are not appointed for a long time, they hurry one another along in succession, each harboring expediency for the moment: their disruptions hinder the people, their expenses injure the people, their lack of intention to remain and consequent carelessness in governance harm the people, and their assumption that they will soon be transferred—seeking only to satisfy their own desires—further distresses the people. Therefore, that long tenure is an excellent method can be determined without even rising from one's seat. Now the Son of Heaven bestows gracious favor upon the black-haired multitude and revitalizes official administration, clearly decreeing that the ministers who hold the balance of personnel selection uniformly make six years the standard term, intending thereby gradually to restore the [Tang and Yu / ancient?] …

title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
周九載之制而一洗近代沿襲之非□宜
吏稱民安烝烝然盛矣而或謂官非積久
固無以定天下之志擢非不次亦無以作
天下之氣是超遷不可不講也又謂守令
得人則久而為利守令非人則久而為害
是考課不可不精也斯其道固然而亦今
日之所嘗參互而並用者愚生復何說以
進哉無亦所以維持久任使行之無弊者
尚有變通神明之方而今殆未之盡歟請
===
掇拾舊聞而執事擇焉漢修輸粟之令則
吏道雜而多端繼拜武功之爵則官職冗
而耗廢今選人得無有似之者乎是仕路
不可不清也宓子宰單父喻掣肘於借書
龔遂治渤海願無拘以文法今才諝得無
有未展者乎是便宜不可不假也虞廷九
官彼此不侵其職漢世諸吏小大不踰其
方今任殊劇易儻亦有材品之當度者乎
撫字誠勞催科拙而逭罰寵辱靡介漕舟

translation_en:
…the system of nine-year assessments of the [Yu and] Zhou, and thoroughly wash away the errors inherited from recent times. Indeed [?], it ought to be that officials are equal to their duties, the people are at peace, and everything flourishes progressively! Yet some say that if offices are not held for a long time, there is truly no way to settle the minds of the empire; and if promotions are not made out of turn, there is likewise no way to rouse the spirit of the empire—thus extraordinary promotion cannot go undiscussed. Others say that if one gets the right men as prefects and magistrates, long tenure brings benefit; if one gets the wrong men as prefects and magistrates, long tenure brings harm—thus the evaluation of merit cannot but be rigorous. These principles are certainly true, and they are also what are already mutually consulted and jointly applied today; what further argument could this foolish student offer to advance the matter? Could it not be that with regard to the means of sustaining long tenure and making it operate without abuse, there are still methods of flexible adaptation and inspired application that today have perhaps not yet been fully exhausted? Allow me to gather up accounts from the past so that Your Excellency may choose among them.

When the Han instituted the ordinances for contributing grain, the paths to officialdom became mixed and multifarious; when they subsequently conferred orders of honour for military merit, official posts became superfluous and went to waste. Among those selected for office today, could it be that there are cases resembling this? Thus the path to officialdom cannot but be purified. When Master Fu [Fu Buqi 宓不齊] governed Shanfu 單父, he illustrated the hindering of his hand by the parable of writing with his elbow pulled back; when Gong Sui 龔遂 governed Bohai 渤海, he asked not to be constrained by legal technicalities. Among men of talent and wisdom today, could it be that there are those who have not been able to unfold their abilities? Thus discretionary authority cannot but be granted. Among the nine officials of the court of Yu [Shun], none encroached upon another's duties; among the various officials of the Han era, great and small did not overstep their bounds. Today, posts differ in being arduous or easy—might there not also be capacities and grades that ought to be measured accordingly? When one is genuinely toiling in nurturing the people, he is pardoned from punishment even if clumsy in pressing for tax collection [referring to Yang Cheng 陽城]; when one is unmoved by favour or disgrace, even if grain transport boats…

title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
失而考優今事涉眚誤儻亦有條格之當
寬者乎綜核詳矣而有戶口僞增勞來蒙
賞以參其間俗吏之虛名寧可禁耶是故
名實宜覈也治理效矣而非璽書勉勵增
秩賜金以示其褒人心之鼓舞能無倦耶
是故旌勸宜行也仕路清則待選者不致
停壅而久任不以出於疏通之計而妨便
宜假則懷才者咸獲展布而久任不以趣
數無由見所長而妨材品度則繁簡適宜
===
鉅細畢舉而久任不以用違其器弗克負
荷而妨條格寬則過者可滌罅者可補而
久任不以苟容求全懷危內顧而妨名實
覈則有功者上無功者下而久任不以真
贋相冒而妨旌異行則賢者益奮滯者弗
嗟而久任不以志意銷沮而妨久任以主
之超遷考課以佐之又有是數者以變通
而神明之官有常人人有常心功程其所
必奏情體其所必至不責望於力分之外

Then offices will have constant incumbents and men will have constant minds; achievements will be assessed by what can surely be accomplished, and circumstances will be understood according to what must naturally occur, neither demanding what lies beyond the limits of their strength…

title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不沮撓於局守之內內堅其濯磨砥礪之
衷外作其感激迅發之氣使人不敢以倖
亦不敢以怠治不流於弛亦不流於擾寓
縣之中清和咸理猶其家政之整頓盈縮
也裨海之遙臂運指從猶其子弟臧獲之
安養服習也即漢世之樞機周密品式備
具豈復要於此哉雖然尤有機焉曰在上
不在下在邇不在遠昔虞何以咸寧萬國
曰以內之百揆四岳統外之州牧侯伯也
===
周何以阜成兆民曰六卿分職各率其屬
以倡九牧也而奚獨疑於今乎是故守令
統之監司監司歸之省院省院平之臺閣
內而給諫臺察也外而部使巡行也則血
脈之周流灌注於榮衞者也欲綱舉目張
必先視諸管鑰之謹守欲源清流潔必先
求諸統紀之畫一此皆積久以課實非能
佹成而偶致者也若上苟且而責下之精
弛近速化而抑遠之躁競胡可得巳蓋嘗

Within the realm and its counties, purity, harmony, and universal order will prevail, just like managing the expansion and contraction of one's own household affairs; as far away as the encircling seas, commands will be executed as the arm moves the fingers, just like the peaceful nurturing and obedient habituation of one's own sons, younger brothers, and household servants. It was through the Six Ministers (liuqing) dividing responsibilities, each leading his subordinates in order to guide the Nine Pastors (jiumu). Why then should we doubt this alone in the present day? Therefore, Prefects and Magistrates are directed by the Surveillance Commissions and Circuits, the Surveillance Commissions and Circuits report to the Ministries and the Censorate, and the Ministries and the Censorate have their deliberations weighed and balanced by the Grand Secretariat. Within the capital, the Supervising Secretaries and Investigating Censors, and outside in the provinces, the touring circuit emissaries—these are like the blood and pulse circulating and infusing vitality throughout the nutritive and defensive systems of the body. 譬之上者表也下者其影乎近者轂也遠
者其輻乎表直而影安從曲轂轉而輻胡
不隨其機固有然者於戲治天下者甞患
法作於上而格於下謹於始而倦於終所
頼知者銳而行之勇者毅而守之規宏遠
不規近小計利害不計人情今幸
明天子主斷於上賢公卿奉持於下久任之行
犂然有緒而黃虞三代之隆可幾而復矣
即有疲執戟歎積薪者陰疾治世之繩墨

…compare it to this: those above are the gnomon, and are not those below its shadow? The near is the hub of the wheel, and is not the distant its spokes? When the gnomon is straight, how can the shadow be crooked? When the hub turns, how can the spokes not follow? Its mechanism is inherently so. Alas! Those who govern the empire have often worried that laws are instituted at the top yet obstructed below, and are observed with care at the beginning yet neglected by the end. What we rely upon is that the wise carry them out with keen determination and the brave guard them with resolute perseverance—planning for what is grand and far-reaching rather than what is near and petty, and calculating real advantages and harms rather than personal sensibilities. title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
國體者歟
夫天下大勢譬人一身京師元首也而朝
廷政令出焉則心也四方四體也體戴夫
首則外有統而其勢尊心運夫體則內有
主而其勢順居尊而達順則重常在我重
常在我然後天下不勞而治自古帝王垂
拱而天下晏如者凡以能制輕重之勢而
加意於本原之地也
國家肇基自南而定鼎於北上應北辰以象
===
天極南面而聽天下謹按輿圖以觀其勢
薊門遼陽上谷雲朔者肩背也河濼咽喉
也伊洛湘漢江淮之間腹也齊魯秦晉左
右手也閩蜀腋也交廣滇粵足也肩背欲
厚咽喉欲通腹欲實左右手腋欲彊足無
跋盭相承而奉元首以聽命於心而心與
元首則又精神所聚會以運用百體而榮
衛灌注焉然後形氣充悅而外邪不奸也
二祖開基

國體者歟！
夫天下大勢，譬人一身：京師，元首也；而朝廷政令出焉，則心也；四方，四體也。體戴夫首，則外有統而其勢尊；心運夫體，則內有主而其勢順。居尊而達順，則重常在我；重常在我，然後天下不勞而治。自古帝王垂拱而天下晏如者，凡以能制輕重之勢，而加意於本原之地也。
國家肇基自南，而定鼎於北，上應北辰，以象天極，南面而聽天下。謹按輿圖以觀其勢：薊門、遼陽、上谷、雲、朔者，肩背也；河、濼，咽喉也；伊、洛、湘、漢、江、淮之間，腹也；齊、魯、秦、晉，左右手也；閩、蜀，腋也；交、廣、滇、粵，足也。肩背欲厚，咽喉欲通，腹欲實，左右手腋欲彊，足無跋盭，相承而奉元首，以聽命於心。而心與元首，則又精神所聚會，以運用百體而榮衛灌注焉，然後形氣充悅而外邪不奸也。二祖開基，
translation_en:
… the fundamental structure of the state!

Now, the overall configuration of the realm may be compared to a human body: the capital is the head; the court, whence government ordinances issue, is the heart-and-mind; and the four quarters are the four limbs. When the limbs support the head above, externally there is unity of command and the position is exalted; when the heart-and-mind directs the limbs, internally there is a master and the movement is harmonious. Occupying an exalted position and achieving harmonious compliance, the weight of authority always rests with us; and when the weight of authority always rests with us, only then is the realm governed without toil. That the emperors and kings of antiquity could let their robes hang down with hands folded while the realm remained tranquil was entirely because they were able to control the balance of light and heavy and pay special heed to the fundamental source.

The dynasty first laid its foundations in the south and established its capital in the north, corresponding above to the Northern Polestar so as to mirror the celestial pole, facing south to give audience to the realm. If we carefully examine the map of the empire to observe its strategic configuration: Jimen, Liaoyang, Shanggu, Yunzhong, and Shuofang are the shoulders and back; the Yellow River and the Luo River [in Shandong, i.e., the Grand Canal corridor] are the throat; the region between the Yi, Luo, Xiang, Han, Yangzi, and Huai rivers is the belly; Qi, Lu, Qin, and Jin are the left and right hands; Min [Fujian] and Shu [Sichuan] are the armpits and flanks; and Jiaozhi, Guangdong, Dian [Yunnan], and Guangxi are the feet. The shoulders and back should be thick, the throat should be unobstructed, the belly should be full, the left and right hands and flanks should be strong, and the feet should be free from stumbling or crookedness, all supporting one another to uphold the head and obey the commands of the heart-and-mind. And the heart-and-mind and the head are in turn where vital spirit gathers and converges, directing the hundred parts of the body and infusing them with nourishing blood and protective qi; only then are the physical form and vital energy full and vigorous, so that external malignancies cannot intrude. The Two Ancestors [Taizu and Taizong] founded the dynasty, …

title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
列聖纘緒逾二百年于茲
朝廷清明百官守職萬姓按堵四夷嚮風可
謂極治矣乃愚所私憂過計不在形體而
在精神明問未之及也夫歲簡九邊之銳
卒以戍薊門徒罷於奔命而止盎然其始
猶曰土兵未練也今練之幾何歲而戍未
盡撤是欲背之厚而不恤肩寒也諉河渠
於不可治而更求便道始猶曰海運可復
也今海舟報罷而河渠如故是不急咽喉
===
之塞而求他竅也伊洛湘漢多曠土江淮
多游民而洛人苦
宗藩淮人苦水潦平居無事常皇皇若不聊
生是枵腹旦夕也齊魯南支河渠秦晉北
支胡西支羌閩蜀交廣滇粵又西南萬里
而支寇寇彌山海民無所號呼頃雖蕩定
如窶人病起休養無所資又虞復病是手
足瘃且倒懸也如此以為安蓋兪扁不顧
聖明在御賢公卿在列豈以內寧而忘外憂夫

多游民而洛人苦
===
宗藩淮人苦水潦平居無事常皇皇若不聊
生是枵腹旦夕也齊魯南支河渠秦晉北
支胡西支羌閩蜀交廣滇粵又西南萬里
而支寇寇彌山海民無所號呼項雖蕩定
如宴人病起休養無所資又虞復病是手
足腋且倒懸也如此以爲安蓋兪扁不顧
聖明在御賢公卿在列豈以內寧而忘外憂夫
punctuated: 列聖纘緒，逾二百年于茲。朝廷清明，百官守職，萬姓按堵，四夷嚮風，可謂極治矣。乃愚所私憂過計，不在形體而在精神，明問未之及也。夫歲簡九邊之銳卒以戍薊門，徒罷於奔命而止盎然，其始猶曰土兵未練也，今練之幾何歲，而戍未盡撤，是欲背之厚而不恤肩寒也；諉河渠於不可治而更求便道，始猶曰海運可復也，今海舟報罷，而河渠如故，是不急咽喉之塞而求他竅也；伊、洛、湘、漢多曠土，江、淮多游民，而洛人苦宗藩，淮人苦水潦，平居無事，常皇皇若不聊生，是枵腹旦夕也；齊、魯南支河渠，秦、晉北支胡、西支羌，閩、蜀、交、廣、滇、粵又西南萬里而支寇，寇彌山海，民無所號呼，頃雖蕩定，如窶人病起，休養無所資，又虞復病，是手足瘃且倒懸也。如此以為安，蓋兪、扁不顧。聖明在御，賢公卿在列，豈以內寧而忘外憂？夫
translation_en:
…and the succession of Sacred Emperors has carried on the heritage for over two hundred years down to the present. The Imperial Court is clear and bright, all officials keep to their duties, the myriad people dwell in peace, and the four barbarian peoples turn toward our civilizing wind—it may truly be called the height of good governance! Yet what I, in my humble ignorance, privately worry and overly fret about lies not in the physical body of the state, but in its vital spirit—something your brilliant inquiry has not yet touched upon.

Now, every year elite troops are selected from the Nine Garrisons to guard Jimen, only to be exhausted by rushing about on orders and ending up depleted [? 止盎然]. At first it was still said that the local troops were not yet trained; now, how many years have they been trained, and still the garrison rotations have not been completely withdrawn? This is wishing the back to be thick while taking no pity on the shoulders growing cold. Blaming the Yellow River and the Grand Canal as impossible to tame and seeking instead a convenient alternative route, at first it was still said that sea transport could be restored; now the sea vessels have been reported discontinued, while the River and Canal remain just as before. This is not rushing to clear a blockage in the throat, while looking instead for some other orifice. Along the Yi, Luo, Xiang, and Han rivers there is much uncultivated land, and between the Yangtze and Huai rivers there are many vagrant people; meanwhile the people of the Luo region suffer from the imperial clansmen’s princely estates, and the people of the Huai suffer from flooding. Even in ordinary times of peace they are constantly anxious as though unable to make a living—this is going with an empty belly from morning to night. Qi and Lu to the south must cope with the River and Canal; Qin and Jin must cope with the northern nomads to the north and the Qiang peoples to the west; and Min, Shu, Jiao, Guang, Dian, and Yue, stretching ten thousand li to the southwest, must cope with bandits. Bandits filled the mountains and seas, leaving the people nowhere to cry out for help; although they have recently been swept clean and pacified, it is like an impoverished man just rising from an illness who has no resources for recuperation and fears falling ill again—this is having hands and feet frostbitten and hanging upside down. To regard such a state as secure is a case that Yu Fu and Bian Que would not even deign to look at. With His Sacred Majesty upon the throne and worthy ministers in the ranks of court, how could one because of internal calm forget external anxieties? Now…

title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
薊門教練取浙卒焉漁陽突騎故甲於天
下豈曰無兵而南取浙居則南兵倍其食
急則北兵當其鋒南驕北怨敗道也頃虜
一小入輒破軍殺將其效可睹已愚以為
不罷浙卒則土兵不成土兵不成則九邊
之戍未得息肩也河故湍悍堤束其流洲
綰其口豪俠貴勢宅菰葦田沮洳以當水
道者有司不敢問以故數治數淤數淤數
決往時坐此迄無成功頃疏草灣報效矣
===
愚以為不併力下流則漕渠不通漕渠不
通則徐淮之民未得安枕也
新政壹務節約帑庾不盈水旱盜賊不加於
往時而皇皇不聊生者舊逋雜征而催科
急也
天子幸哀憐小民不待建白一旦而下緩征之
詔民鼓舞若更生矣諺曰東南熟天下足東
南之粟轉轂贍天下而交廣江淮創夷昏
墊之民終歲不復喁喁待澤其它山徼海

translation_en:
…military training at Jimen recruits soldiers from Zhejiang for the purpose. The charging cavalry of Yuyang have historically been the finest in the realm; how could it be said that there are no soldiers there, that we must look south to recruit from Zhejiang? In peacetime, the southern soldiers receive double the rations; in emergencies, the northern soldiers bear the brunt of the enemy's spearhead. The southerners grow arrogant while the northerners grow resentful—this is a path to defeat. Recently, whenever the northern caitiffs make even a minor incursion, they rout our armies and slay our generals; the results of this policy can already be seen. In my humble opinion, unless the Zhejiang soldiers are dismissed, the local troops will not be properly formed; and unless the local troops are properly formed, the garrisons of the Nine Frontiers will never be able to rest their shoulders.

The Yellow River is naturally swift and violent. Dikes constrict its current and sandbars choke its mouth, while powerful magnates and noble families build estates among the reeds and cultivate the marshlands right in the path of the water's course, and the authorities dare not question them. For this reason, the more frequently it is dredged, the more frequently it silts up, and the more frequently it silts up, the more frequently it breaches its banks; in the past, because of this, efforts have ultimately achieved no success. Recently, the dredging of Caowan has yielded reported success. Yet in my humble opinion, unless we concentrate our strength on the lower reaches, the Grand Canal will not flow freely; and unless the Grand Canal flows freely, the people of Xuzhou and Huaian will never be able to sleep in peace.

The new administration has devoted itself single-mindedly to economy and frugality, even before the treasuries and granaries are full. Floods, droughts, and banditry are no worse than in former times, yet the people are anxious and lack the means to make a living because old tax arrears are compounded by miscellaneous levies and the collection of taxes is pressed with urgency. Fortunately, the Son of Heaven took pity on the common people; without waiting for memorials to be submitted, he issued an edict in a single day deferring tax collection, and the people rejoiced with dancing as though given a new lease on life. As the proverb says, "When the Southeast has a ripe harvest, the whole realm has enough." The grain of the Southeast is transported by cart and boat to sustain the entire realm, while the wounded and flood-stricken people of Jiaozhi, Guangdong, Guangxi, the Yangtze, and the Huai receive no relief the whole year round, gazing up eagerly as they wait for imperial grace; and as for the other mountain frontiers and coastal…

title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
撫
君門萬里民懸命於有司此尤當念愚以為不
覈實有司則
德意不宣德意不宣則窮陬遐壤之民未得被
澤也然此皆末論非本原至計夫順天八
郡於周為燕趙諸國於唐為成德盧龍魏
博范陽等軍當是時各阡陌其地什伍其
民無庸外助今其地與民猶昔也而班操
上徐豫之軍漕輓籍江淮之粟旁引百郡
以為助而猶不足乃欲開京東瀕海萑葦
之塲用浙人築隄捍水之法聽富民田其
中合衆分地計畝授官此元臣虞集之議
也然洪武中蓋有開荒田土永不起科之
令矣其後荆棘未盡剪而有司者輒履畝
而稅之矣抑或田成業定而中貴外戚輒
請為已業而豪奪之矣如此尚有應令者
乎愚以為今即不能如令第募民田以三
年起輕科而信守之豈惟京東將隙地無
alt_text:
懦
右門萬里民懸命於有司此尤當念愚以爲不
德意不宜德意不宜則窮陬遐壤之民未得被
澤也然此皆末論非本原至計夫順天八
郡於周爲燕趙諸國於唐爲成德盧龍魏
博范陽等軍當是時各阡陌其地什伍其
民無庸外助今其地與民猶昔也而班操
上徐豫之軍漕輓籍江淮之粟旁引百郡
===
以爲助而猶不足乃欲開京東瀕海萑葦
之塲用浙人築隄捍水之法聽富民田其
中合衆分地計畝授官此元臣虞集之議
也然洪武中嘗有開荒田土永不起科之
令矣其後荆棘未盡剪而有司者輒履畝
而稅之矣抑或田成業定而中貴外戚輒
請爲己業而豪奪之矣如此尚有應令者
乎愚以爲今即不能如令第募民田以三
年起輕科而信守之豈惟京東將隙地無
punctuated: 撫，君門萬里，民懸命於有司，此尤當念。愚以為不覈實有司，則德意不宣；德意不宣，則窮陬遐壤之民未得被澤也。然此皆末論，非本原至計。夫順天八郡，於周為燕、趙諸國，於唐為成德、盧龍、魏博、范陽等軍。當是時，各阡陌其地，什伍其民，無庸外助。今其地與民猶昔也，而班操上徐、豫之軍，漕輓籍江、淮之粟，旁引百郡以為助而猶不足。乃欲開京東瀕海萑葦之塲，用浙人築隄捍水之法，聽富民田其中，合衆分地，計畝授官，此元臣虞集之議也。然洪武中蓋有開荒田土永不起科之令矣，其後荆棘未盡剪，而有司者輒履畝而稅之矣；抑或田成業定，而中貴、外戚輒請為已業而豪奪之矣。如此，尚有應令者乎？愚以為今即不能如令，第募民田，以三年起輕科而信守之，豈惟京東，將隙地無
translation_en:
… marches [?], the gate of the sovereign is ten thousand li away, and the people's very lives hang upon the local authorities; this especially ought to be kept in mind. In my humble opinion, if we do not verify the actual performance of the local authorities, the sovereign's benevolent intentions will not be proclaimed; and if his benevolent intentions are not proclaimed, the people of impoverished corners and distant regions will not be able to receive his grace. Yet all of these are superficial discussions, not the ultimate plan addressing the fundamental source.

Now, the eight prefectures of the Shuntian region were, in the Zhou dynasty, the various states of Yan and Zhao, and in the Tang dynasty, the military commands of Chengde, Lulong, Weibo, Fanyang, and so forth. At that time, each laid out its own lands into ridged fields and organized its own people into units of five and ten, having no need of outside assistance. Today, the land and the people are the same as in the past, yet for rotational training we bring up troops from Xuzhou and Henan, and for canal transport we rely on grain from the Yangtze and Huai regions, drawing upon a hundred prefectures on all sides for assistance—and still it is not enough.

Thus, there is the proposal to open up the coastal reed-marshes east of the capital, employing the method of the people of Zhejiang for building dikes to hold back the water, allowing wealthy commoners to cultivate the land within, pooling crowds to divide the land, and bestowing official rank calculated according to the acreage reclaimed; this was the proposal of the Yuan-dynasty official Yu Ji 虞集. However, during the Hongwu reign (1368–1398) there was indeed an ordinance that newly reclaimed wasteland would never be assessed for land tax. Afterward, before the brambles had even been completely cleared, the local authorities would already pace off the acres and tax them; or else, once the fields were completed and the property established, palace eunuchs and imperial relatives by marriage would request them as their own estates and seize them by force. Under such circumstances, would there still be anyone to answer the call of the ordinance? In my humble opinion, even if today we cannot match that original ordinance, if we simply recruit commoners to cultivate the land, begin levying a light tax after three years, and faithfully abide by this promise, then not only in the region east of the capital, but throughout the vacant lands there will be none…

title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不可耕者且使粟價無踊游民有歸萬世
之利也又欲倣漢唐置三輔宋四輔郡意
東永平西易州南臨清北宣府各宿重兵
二萬而罷直隸河南山東班軍此先臣丘
濬之議也顧安所得兵若募市人徒益餽
餉緩急不可恃若籍民丁前代蓋有名寓
於農而實編於官者矣既編於官後必勾
補又或有調征移戍者矣是亡辜坐謫也
蓋洪武中太平諸郡數蠲田租海內不以
===
===
為私若曰此吾湯沐邑緩急共之愚以為
誠舉四輔赤子付之良有司俾悉心愛養
勿撓以貴勢而又寬其徭賦時加惠焉稍
以其閒分曹角射課藝習兵民業既成皆
安土樂生而戴其上雖不設四輔隱然保
障之固亦萬世之利也至若三營精銳國
之威也半雜老弱而敝裝羸馬四方逋逃
民之賊也羣萃淵藪而作奸犯科甚非所
以重

民之賊也羣萃淵藪而作奸犯科甚非所

punctuated: 不可耕者，且使粟價無踊，游民有歸，萬世之利也。又欲倣漢、唐置三輔，宋四輔郡意，東永平、西易州、南臨清、北宣府，各宿重兵二萬，而罷直隸、河南、山東班軍，此先臣丘濬之議也。顧安所得兵？若募市人，徒益餽餉，緩急不可恃；若籍民丁，前代蓋有名寓於農而實編於官者矣，既編於官，後必勾補，又或有調征移戍者矣，是亡辜坐謫也。蓋洪武中，太平諸郡數蠲田租，海內不以為私，若曰：「此吾湯沐邑，緩急共之。」愚以為誠舉四輔赤子付之良有司，俾悉心愛養，勿撓以貴勢，而又寬其徭賦，時加惠焉，稍以其閒分曹角射，課藝習兵。民業既成，皆安土樂生而戴其上，雖不設四輔，隱然保障之固，亦萬世之利也。至若三營精銳，國之威也，半雜老弱，而敝裝羸馬；四方逋逃，民之賊也，羣萃淵藪，而作奸犯科，甚非所以重
translation_en: … cannot be cultivated; moreover, it would keep grain prices from soaring and give vagrant people a place to settle—a benefit for ten thousand generations. There is also the proposal to imitate the Han and Tang establishment of the Three Metropolitan Areas (Sanfu) and the Song intention in setting up the Four Auxiliary Prefectures (Sifujun), stationing a heavy force of twenty thousand troops at each of Yongping in the east, Yizhou in the west, Linqing in the south, and Xuanfu in the north, while abolishing the rotational troops from the Metropolitan Area (Zhili), Henan, and Shandong. This was the proposal of the former official Qiu Jun 丘濬. Yet where would the soldiers be obtained? If townspeople are recruited, it will merely increase the burden of provisioning and they cannot be relied upon in emergencies. If civilian males are registered, in former dynasties there were indeed cases where they were nominally lodged among the peasantry yet in reality enrolled on official military registers; once enrolled on the official registers, replacements will inevitably be conscripted later, and they may even be transferred for distant campaigns or shifted to frontier garrisons—which is to suffer the punishment of exile though innocent of any crime. During the Hongwu reign (1368–1398), land taxes were repeatedly remitted in Taiping and neighboring prefectures, and the realm did not regard this as partiality, as if to say: “These are our bath-towns (royal appanages), which share with us both peace and crisis.” I humbly believe that if we truly entrust the people of the four auxiliary regions to capable local officials, having them wholeheartedly cherish and nurture them without interference from the powerful and noble, while also lightening their corvée and taxes and periodically bestowing favors upon them, and in their spare time gradually dividing them into groups to compete in archery and testing their skills in military training—then once the people’s livelihoods are secure, all will be content on their land, take joy in their lives, and revere their superiors. Even without formally establishing Four Auxiliary Prefectures, there will be an unseen yet solid bulwark, which is likewise a benefit for ten thousand generations. As for the elite troops of the Three Great Training Divisions (Sanying), they are the majesty of the state, yet half are mingled with the old and weak, with tattered gear and emaciated horses; fugitives from all quarters are the bane of the people, yet they gather in this haven to commit evil and violate the laws. title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
京師而示天下也今歲時簡練團營精采固
已改觀而市井游惰尚多竊匿蒐而逐之
則傷覆載之仁保而容之則滋奸宄之黨
愚以為此二事者乃金吾巡徼戎臣開府
一有司之事耳而
國家之精神不與焉夫齊秦霸臣尚能保伍
其民令無匿奸李光弼為將而旌旗壁壘
皆變是故精神誠通凡此類者皆不問而
舉今
朝廷下尺檄而中外諸吏恐懼奔走此乃形
體相攝屬而非精神所流貫故法嚴令具
而
輦轂之下且有令之不行禁之不止者又何
以責四方是故明目達聰開誠廣益時
召公卿坐論治理間引郡縣親對便宜燭閭
閻於衿帶運要荒於几席使上之情常通
於下如星辰之垂象而易知下之情常通
於上如聲響之乘虛而易達然後天下之

translation_en: … the capital and display it to the empire. Now, through seasonal inspection and training, the vigor of the Integrated Divisions (tuanying) has indeed taken on a new appearance, yet among the idlers in the marketplaces, many still hide in secret. To search them out and expel them would injure the benevolence that covers and sustains all things like heaven and earth; to protect and tolerate them would breed factions of villains and traitors. In my humble opinion, these two matters are merely the business of a single functionary—the Imperial Bodyguard (Jinwu) patrolling the beats, or the military commanders opening their headquarters—and the vital spirit of the state does not reside therein. Even the ministers of the hegemons of Qi and Qin were able to organize their people into five-household mutual-security groups so that no villains could be concealed; when Li Guangbi李光弼 became general, the very banners, flags, and ramparts were all transformed. Therefore, if the vital spirit truly circulates, all matters of this sort are accomplished without even asking. Nowadays, when the court sends down a one-foot dispatch, all the officials inside and outside the capital rush about in fear and trembling; this is merely physical subordination and control, not the pervading flow of vital spirit. Thus, even though the laws are strict and ordinances complete, right beneath the imperial chariot wheels there are still orders that are not carried out and prohibitions that do not stop offenses—how then can one hold the four quarters accountable? Therefore, the ruler should see clearly and hear afar, open his heart in sincerity and broaden the benefits of counsel, frequently summon the dukes and ministers to sit and discuss the principles of governance, and from time to time bring in prefectural and county officials to answer in person regarding what is advantageous and appropriate; he should illuminate the common folk within the folds of his robes and girdle, and maneuver the distant borderlands from his desk and mat. title: 萬曆四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
勢聯合為一身無復有擁閼者雖尺寸之
膚癬疥之疾心所拊循手不待命而至首
所嚮往足不煩諭而行此所謂不在形體
而在精神者明問未之及也愚何敢畢其
說

punctuated: 勢聯合為一身，無復有擁閼者。雖尺寸之膚、癬疥之疾，心所拊循，手不待命而至；首所嚮往，足不煩諭而行。此所謂不在形體而在精神者，明問未之及也，愚何敢畢其說？
translation_en: …conditions will be united into a single body, and there will no longer be anything obstructed or blocked. Even if there is an ailment of ringworm or scabies on a mere inch or foot of skin, where the mind seeks to soothe, the hand arrives without waiting for a command; where the head turns its inclination, the feet move without the trouble of an instruction. This is what is meant by depending not on the physical form, but on the vital spirit. Your enlightened question did not touch upon this, yet how could I, in my foolishness, dare not set forth my explanation to the end?
